questions.Subject: Economics

questions.Subject: Economics
questions.Topic: Factors of Production and Production Possibility Curve
questions.Question: Why is the Production Possibility Curve (PPC) typically CONCAVE to the origin (bowed outwards)?

questions.Explanation: Resources are specialized (imperfect substitutes). Shifting resources from one good to another requires transferring increasingly less suitable inputs, increasing marginal opportunity cost.

questions.Subject: Economics
questions.Topic: Factors of Production and Production Possibility Curve
questions.Question: What does any point situated INSIDE (below) the Production Possibility Curve indicate about an economy?
questions.OptionA: The economy is operating at its maximum technological potential
questions.OptionB: The economy has attained full employment with zero inflation

questions.Explanation: Points inside the PPC represent productive inefficiency or idle resources (e.g. high unemployment, idle factories); output could be increased without sacrificing other goods.

questions.Subject: Economics
questions.Topic: Factors of Production and Production Possibility Curve
questions.Question: What does a point situated OUTSIDE (beyond) the Production Possibility Curve represent?
questions.OptionA: An inefficient point with mass unemployment

questions.Option_d: An output combination that is currently unattainable given the economy's existing resources and technology
questions.Explanation: Points beyond the frontier are impossible to attain with current resources and technology; they can only be reached through economic growth or international trade.

questions.Subject: Economics
questions.Topic: Factors of Production and Production Possibility Curve

questions.Subject: Economics
